candidateDecisions.label: Cultural Heritage, Museums and Public Memory
Excavation, archaeological science & bioarchaeology
candidateDecisions.assessment: The current workbook supports introductory archaeological inference, Greek material culture, spatial analysis and soils. These contributions cannot sustain a separate laboratory and field archaeology pathway with repeated excavation, finds processing, archaeological material analysis or specialist work on plant, animal and human remains.

analysis: Both plans use the three UCR archaeology and ancient-heritage courses as a substantive base. World Archaeology examines craft, settlement, exchange and material evidence; Greek Archaeology concentrates on material traces of community and democracy; Heritage & Ancient Democracy extends analysis of Athenian civic life and its later interpretation. The ancient societies plan adds Mediterranean exchange, myths and texts, history of empires, ancient warfare, GIS and soils. Environmental surveying and spatial data teach transferable techniques; excavation and archaeological lab interpretation remain absent. The heritage plan adds rhetoric, community communication, sociology, qualitative inquiry and ethics to museums, restitution, heritage and documentary work. Modern museums, African Art & Heritage and media analysis support the institutional strand. The remaining shared advanced research courses teach art-historical, literary, historical and media inquiry, with Researching the American Century used for the historical method and explicit contextual limits. The revised alignments retain four specific areas of overlap. There is no defensible separate archaeological science or excavation plan.
